hero.headline: The agentic software platform.
hero.ledePrimary: Production infrastructure for software your AI builds. Three products designed end-to-end so the result is a real shippable app, not a prototype.
hero.ledeSecondary: The way software gets made is changing. The product builder is not a coder; they are a thinker with an AI. The platform that runs what they build should be designed for that — not retrofitted from a decade ago.

items.title: The product builder is not a coder.
items.body: The person shipping software now is a thinker with an AI in front of them. They review what gets written; they rarely write it themselves. The platform underneath needs to be designed for that shape of work, not retrofitted from a decade ago.

items.title: Prototype quality is the floor, not the bar.
items.body: Vibe-coding tools spin up a working demo in minutes. That's now table stakes. The work that matters is what comes after: a real database, real data, real users, real revisions, real production. That's where the platform earns its keep.

items.title: Glue is the bottleneck — not the model.
items.body: Every team building seriously with AI assembles the same stack: a data layer, a database, a hosting target, a CI flow, a preview environment. Each piece works; the seams don't. The model is great. The integration tax is where the weeks go.

items.title: The PR is the new build artifact.
items.body: You don't ship code. You ship a working product — a URL with a real database behind it that a non-technical person can actually try. The unit of work is a previewable, mergeable pull request. Production becomes the path of least resistance.

items.title: Schemas are the contract AI must respect.
items.body: Your AI can write almost anything. What it can't do is silently break production data. A platform that takes the schema seriously — typed end-to-end, branchable per PR, shadowed for safe diffs — is what lets the AI ship without anyone flinching.

items.title: One platform. One config. One bill.
items.body: You shouldn't be navigating five dashboards to ship something your AI built in three minutes. The platform should compose into a single typed file your AI can read, your team can review, and your invoice doesn't fragment across.

platform.headline: So we built one.
platform.body: Three products — Prisma Data for the data layer, Prisma Compute for hosting, Prisma Postgres for the database — composed into one platform. Designed end-to-end so the result is a real, previewable, shippable product.

products.label: 01 · Build
products.title: Prisma Data
products.body: Your AI reads, writes, and migrates schemas. Typed end-to-end, safe by default.

products.label: 02 · Deploy
products.title: Prisma Compute
products.body: TypeScript on Bun. Repo to URL in seconds. Your agent deploys, reads logs, fixes itself.

products.label: 03 · Store
products.title: Prisma Postgres
products.body: Real Postgres. Every branch gets one — seeded, queryable, mergeable.

products.label: 04 · Ship
products.title: Previews & production
products.body: Every PR becomes a working app. Review the UI, the data, the deploy — then merge.

platform.footRight: one platform · one CLI · one bill

exhibit.headline: The whole thing, in one typed file.
exhibit.bodyPrimary: Not a dashboard. Not a YAML matrix. A TypeScript module that lives next to your code, ships with your repo, and changes through pull requests like everything else.
exhibit.bodySecondary: Your AI reads it to plan. The platform reads it to provision. You read it to understand what's running. There is no other source of truth.
exhibit.footnote: "AGENTS.md" tells your AI how the codebase works. "prisma.config.ts" tells the platform. Both are versioned. Neither is a secret.
